subject: Literature
title: Rumi and Sufi Mystical Poetry
description: One-minute skill: Rumi and Sufi Mystical Poetry.

hook.text: Rumi is the best-selling poet in America today, eight centuries after his death in thirteenth-century Persia.

buildup.text: His poetry expresses the ecstatic union between the human soul and the divine through images of wine, dance, and love.

discovery.text: Rumi began writing poetry after meeting the wandering mystic Shams of Tabriz, who transformed his entire worldview.

twist.text: Many popular English translations strip Rumi's poetry of its Islamic context, turning Sufi mysticism into generic self-help.

climax.text: Rumi's poetry bridges cultures and centuries, proving that spiritual longing speaks a universal human language.

punchline.text: A medieval Persian mystic outsells modern American poets.

quiz.question: What problem affects popular English translations of Rumi?
options: They are too academic for general readers
They strip his poetry of its Islamic context, turning it into generic self-help
They translate from the wrong original language
